findings.title: Fresh authorization after an expired or ambiguous NOVO attempt submits into its occupied slot
findings.rationale: Blocking current-contract recovery defect, established statically; no runtime reproduction was attempted. In web-app/src/componentes/CadastroNumero.tsx:521-529, the advertised 'Iniciar nova autorização para esta Business Unit' action accepts EXPIRED and AMBIGUOUS_CODE_EXCHANGE but sets canal=null whenever the original attempt.operation was NOVO. The next submit at :272-275 therefore sends operation:NOVO for the same BU. The API expiry paths at api-app/src/domain/channels/number-registration.service.ts:172-174 and :454-456, and ambiguous exchange at :205-207, preserve the attempt's channelId and its BuChannel. Consequently :113-114 deterministically rejects that next request with CHANNEL_SLOT_OCCUPIED. This affects a normal first onboarding that times out or expires, including a BU just created by the wizard; it is not a tenant escape or a request to weaken slot uniqueness. The browser restart proof at web-app/e2e/number-onboarding.spec.ts:273-279 only follows pre-effect cancellation, where the server has actually detached/deleted the slot. The API ambiguous-code proof at api-app/test/number-onboarding-flow.e2e-spec.ts:94-111 correctly uses REAUTORIZAR and therefore does not exercise this consumer mismatch. D-03/D-05 and REG-SEC-06 explicitly require a new attempt/nonce and recovery in the existing BU. A user can manually select the retained channel through the existing form, but the dedicated recovery action currently leads to an avoidable conflict, so that workaround does not establish the promised recovery path.
findings.suggested_action: A (recommended): derive the fresh attempt operation from the current safe BU/channel projection and retained channelId, using the existing REAUTORIZAR contract with that exact channel and current expectedGeneration when the slot is retained; use NOVO when it was actually released. Preserve new Idempotency-Key, attempt and nonce, current ADMIN/session checks, and existing active credentials. B: transactionally release a reservation only when no external effect is conclusively possible, then use NOVO; this is a broader change and must not delete a potentially partial external resource. C: rely on manual channel selection; reject for delivery because the dedicated recovery action remains broken. Add a real BFF/session/PostgreSQL browser regression for an initial NOVO expiry and an initial NOVO ambiguous exchange, drive the advertised recovery action, and assert a fresh 201 attempt/nonce in the same BU without duplicate BU/channel, code replay or active-credential replacement. Capture the discriminating failure before the correction; do not relabel the existing cancellation test as this proof.

findings.title: Required tenant-selection and OUT/renewal adversarial simulations remain incomplete
findings.rationale: Blocking verification debt under VAL-08/DOD-08 and the required attack-simulation decision; this is not a reproduced security exploit. The frozen validation plan's REG-SEC-01, 10 and 11 require discriminating boundary evidence that cannot be inferred from the total green test count. REG-SEC-01: api-app/test/number-onboarding-typebot.e2e-spec.ts:33-45 creates its own matching trigger first, creates the foreign global trigger second, and installs an already-foreign session that makes execution stop before outbound work; :47-60 has only the own-tenant trigger. The unit bridge returns mocked trigger rows without honoring the tenant predicate. These tests prove the foreign-session guard and an own-tenant positive, but do not discriminate the original unscoped trigger-selection defect with a foreign matching global trigger ordered ahead of the correct tenant's trigger and no foreign-session short circuit. REG-SEC-10: api-app/test/atendimento.e2e-spec.ts:198-244 genuinely starts verified and exercises RENEW versus old ingress, but asserts Message absence without the specified complete new-epoch/old-verify sequence. api-app/test/number-onboarding-flow.e2e-spec.ts:489-508 starts from an unverified initial pairing; :524-544 exercises open/connecting on that initial unverified round; :636-684 covers initial pre-identity and divergent-phone cases. No named frozen test holds an old unofficial identity verification across renewal/lease replacement and releases it against the new epoch, or performs the specified new-epoch old-wuid/Y-quarantine/current-X retry sequence with all forbidden side effects checked. REG-SEC-11: BFF/public/Typebot have useful authenticated echo-inside-send, sender-first and later-duplicate proofs, but no concurrent same-key OUT-echo simulation was found; the Promise.all case at number-onboarding-message-acceptance.e2e-spec.ts:43-51 is IN. Current source has the expected tenant predicate, epoch/CAS fences and shared unique acceptance, so these omissions alone do not demonstrate a bypass. However, required simulations have no approved exception in this package and cannot be closed as fully executed. This is a source/assertion-based completeness finding against the current final gate, not an automatic reopening of historical NUM-ARCH/NUM-CRIT or NUM-API-16 labels.
findings.suggested_action: A (recommended): complete a bounded set of the already approved PostgreSQL/provider-double tests: an earlier foreign global trigger competing with an own global trigger and observed bot/resource/session owner; a verified managed channel RENEW with an old verify response retained through epoch replacement plus the specified new-round negative/positive identity sequence; concurrent authenticated OUT echoes sharing one provider key with sender-result enrichment. Preserve the existing tests and assert no foreign text/session/credential, no stale raw content/Message/receipt/unread/realtime/bot effects, and the same final Message.id/createdAt/trusted author with one physical OUT. Reuse current harness barriers and permitted test paths; do not run ad hoc provider or device probes during review. B: obtain an explicit narrowly justified exception from the governing authority, listing each unexecuted scenario and revisit condition; none is present now. C: infer these results from source inspection or the 492 passing tests; reject because it changes required simulation into an implicit waiver. This needs targeted evidence and affected-lane review, not a new architecture or unlimited permutation testing.

overall_assessment:

The approved architecture itself remains appropriate and is substantially implemented. I found no demonstrated current cross-tenant credential substitution, webhook authentication bypass, premature Evolution content acceptance or global customer-token fallback in the reviewed source. That is a bounded review conclusion, not proof that vulnerabilities are absent. Known NUM-PERF-01 is separately accepted as a real blocker; I acknowledge its missing reverse current_channel_id index without duplicating its card. Overall completion remains blocked independently by the disclosed real-provider authorization/pairing/IN/OUT and recovery evidence.

Decision adherence, assessed individually: D-01 is locally supported by atomic BU creation/grant inheritance, BU-row phone comparison/claim and immutable provider ownership, including the cross-transport phone race in number-onboarding-flow.e2e-spec.ts:409. D-02 is locally supported by honest capability checks including explicit Graph version, owned SDK callback and provider-verified app/scopes/WABA/selected page; real Embedded Signup and app allowlists remain unproved. D-03 is structurally supported by scoped persisted attempts, unique tenant/key and BU/type slot, one-use nonce/code, separate candidate/active envelopes, short transactions and attempt/generation/active-version/lease checks at promotion; its normal NOVO recovery consumer fails as reported. D-04 is locally supported by AES-256-GCM with fresh 96-bit nonces and purpose/provider/BU/channel/generation/attempt-or-version AAD, private key loading and fail-closed decryption. Code/PIN stay in component memory and POST bodies; no new browser storage or global token path was found. D-05 has separate authorization, number proof, optional register, subscription and receipt; ambiguous mutations are durably pending and are not blindly replayed. The initial failed/expired authorization recovery action still needs correction. No callback takeover API was introduced. D-06 uses pinned Evolution 2.3.7/digest, stable channel+epoch identities, POST ADMIN/CSRF pairing, durable managed-lifecycle authority distinct from backfill, trust reset before network and current-ownPhone proof before content. Source defenses are sound in this review, but the complete required renewal simulation and actual device proof remain open. D-07 separates registration/provider/receipt dimensions, keeps tombstone ownership and uses local CAS/identity locks; lists are DB-only and close removes send readiness. A provider event is not treated as proof of our originating generation. D-08 routes BFF/public/Typebot through the scoped resolver and one keyed MessageAcceptanceService with PostgreSQL uniqueness and trusted-sender enrichment; Typebot derives tenant from the verified BU. Remaining selection/concurrent-OUT simulation gaps are in NUM-SEC-CP21-02. Public response/window contracts remain in their existing controllers. D-09 is supported by distinct operator and destructive-validation projects/DBs/networks, no fixture ports, a single loopback gateway and a process-bound temporary HTTPS tunnel; actual provider proof remains a separate gate. D-10 is consistent with the recorded serialized STOP/handoffs and direct principal source receipts; this review made no source/Git/runtime changes and does not claim source commits or closeout are already complete.

Module consistency: integrations-and-channels retains adapters and deterministic safe errors, scoped credentials, bounded explicit operations, immutable resource ownership and the narrow migrated official reauthorization exception. That exception requires exact same BU/channel/phone, fresh Meta proof, current authorization and no active credential, with managed trust activated at final promotion; unmanaged Evolution remains unadopted and unverified/undeleted. identity-and-tenancy preserves distinct session/public/service/webhook authentication and current role checks; the new-BU transaction preserves founder and sector grant semantics. inbox-and-conversations owns the unique resource/message key, winner-only domain effects and sender/echo reconciliation while preserving the approved timeline and conversation BU/contact contract. Audit catalog/coverage and current actor attribution preserve BU/tenant/stage metadata without candidate secrets; raw Meta persistence is per verified change/value. Durable architectural decisions are already in module owners, whose Verified status correctly remains pending final acceptance. Constitution, future new-conversation/history stories and existing nullable legacy message identities are preserved; no generic vault, worker, outbox or legacy-adoption platform is needed for this review's fixes.

Security-adversarial decision: risk HIGH for the whole auth/credential/tenant/ingress slice; attack simulation REQUIRED. Existing isolated PG/browser and controlled gateway/provider-header/log/HTTPS evidence supply substantial safe simulation, but the missing named cases in NUM-SEC-CP21-02 prevent full simulation closure. No approved exception was found. The medium risk/recommended-simulation conclusion in the dependency-only diagnostic is an input for its narrower reachability question and does not downgrade this full gate.

Attack surfaces and concrete hypotheses reviewed: (1) anonymous gateway, JSON/form parser and BFF/public/service prefixes: parser limits and distinct surface middleware were inspected; an absent session, wrong role or foreign resource must fail before provider side effects or revealing state. Existing HTTP tests exercise those denials, and raw tagged SQL/Prisma predicates introduce no identified injection path. (2) same-site browser cookies and custom-header CSRF: session signature, active-user/password checks, exact CORS configuration, POST-only pair and retired GET were inspected and simulated. (3) OAuth/SDK code injection, replay, stale popup and hostile resource IDs: current operation ownership plus server-bound session/nonce/CAS and app/scoped-resource verification counter these hypotheses; postMessage ingestion was removed. Real SDK/authorization behavior is still external evidence. (4) candidate substitution, wrong purpose/owner/generation and key/tamper failures: crypto and PG tests counter these locally. (5) provider egress and partial effects: fixed Graph origin, encoded resource paths, opaque bounded cursor, redirect:error, 10-second timeouts, <=3 registration requests per round, 45-second channel lease, no HTTP inside transactions and no automatic replay of ambiguous mutation counter redirect/SSRF/replay paths in the touched adapters. Evolution URLs are installation configuration, not operator-provided request destinations. (6) forged or late webhook, mixed-owner batch and pre-identity content: raw-body HMAC for Meta, timing-safe private Evolution header, exact identity lookup, per-epoch mapping and the final shared identity lock counter the attacks; complete renewal simulation is still missing. (7) duplicate IN/OUT/echo and forged authorship: resource-scoped unique acceptance rolls back loser conversation/unread effects and permits enrichment only from authenticated sender results; concurrent OUT echo evidence still needs completion. (8) Typebot tenant breakout/session smuggling: tenant-filtered trigger lookup and session owner checks exist, but the competing-global-trigger simulation is not discriminating as currently arranged. Typebot receives message data; this slice introduces no LLM agent, prompt interpreter or tool invocation authority, so no new prompt-to-tool attack surface was identified. (9) secret exfiltration through diagnostics, URL logs, traces, build contexts and public assets: redaction, public projections, trace/screenshot/video-off onboarding tests, Docker exclusions, source masks and bounded actual logging proofs were inspected. (10) dependency and availability abuse: exact advisory prerequisites were assessed separately below. These hypotheses are classified as countered by source/existing safe simulation, partially simulated, or unverified as stated; none is silently counted as a fresh runtime reproduction.

REG-SEC boundary assessment: 01 PARTIAL simulation: foreign-session rejection and own-tenant positive are supported; adversarial ordering of competing global triggers is missing as reported. The three-caller credential PG test observes distinct resource/token pairs and uses a wrong-resource negative, rather than a predicate-free mock alone. 02 LOCALLY SUPPORTED: sequential/ten-concurrent x3 deliveries, distinct-resource same-ID controls, ID-less rejection, one physical Message/unread and Meta downstream counts are present; unique acceptance applies to both transports. No external exactly-once promise is inferred. 03 LOCALLY SUPPORTED: creation-time pre-identity IN returns 503 with metadata only and zero Message/conversation, ownPhone mismatch quarantines, exact-phone proof permits the same-key retry, and @lid is rejected in source. These are synthetic identities, not device proof. 04 LOCALLY SUPPORTED: removal retains immutable owner, a different BU is denied before register, and late old-resource content creates no Message/conversation; the DB trigger prevents provider/resource/BU rewrite. 05 LOCALLY SUPPORTED: retired GET QR has zero provider delta, missing-CSRF POST is denied before channel/provider effects, ADMIN pair uses the leased generation path. 06 MIXED: exact migrated credentialless official reauthorization, wrong-owner negatives, one-use/ambiguous code and fresh nonce via REAUTORIZAR are supported on the backend; the advertised initial NOVO recovery consumer is broken. No WHATSAPP_TOKEN fallback exists. 07 LOCALLY SUPPORTED WITH BOUNDED EVIDENCE: wrong-phone/cancelled/expired/superseded candidate preservation/erasure and stale-attempt/lease controls are present; source promotion rechecks currentAttempt, generation, active version and lease through DB mutation. This does not prove every possible scheduling permutation. 08 LOCALLY SUPPORTED FOR THE EXERCISED SURFACES: recursive redaction/URL tests, scoped diagnostic persistence and actual gateway/application/provider log scans provide useful positive metadata plus secret-marker negatives. Pre-identity content is excluded; actual QR and OAuth/PIN sessions have not been exercised, so their real-provider artifact hygiene is still pending. 09 LOCALLY SUPPORTED CRYPTO/TRANSPORT DESIGN, EXTERNAL STEP PENDING: candidate and active AAD dimensions, tamper/missing key, no-global-token, code-in-POST and redirect controls are tested. Restricted source scan found no new secret browser-storage/URL sink. Trace/screenshot/video are disabled for onboarding tests. Actual HTTPS login/cookie round trip proves the configured transport, not an actual code/PIN submission. 10 PARTIAL simulation: old ingress versus verified-channel retirement/renewal and source epoch/CAS fences are supported, but the required complete old-verify/new-epoch sequence and forbidden-side-effect observations remain missing. 11 PARTIAL simulation: real BFF/public/Typebot entry paths deliver authenticated echo during send and preserve the same ID/createdAt/trusted content/author, and existing Inbox refresh shows one line; sender-first and later duplicate are exercised. Concurrent OUT echoes are not. 12 LOCALLY SUPPORTED: old path authentication returns 410, correct/wrong header boundaries, challenge acceptance/rejection/rotation and actual gateway 200/403/504/400 parser/upstream cases have named safe proofs. Pinned provider-origin header 200/403 with qrcode:false and separate gateway-to-actual-API header 200/403 are distinct evidence. The earlier inherited Nginx sink leak is acknowledged; the final effective configuration disables it and token rotation/zero-secret scans support current remediation. The nonsecret /probe-callback marker in provider error logs is intentionally retained and is not an installation-secret leak. 13 LOCALLY SUPPORTED: original signature is checked before partitioning; each verified change/value is persisted under its owner, unknown/retired fragments are dropped without content, and the signed mixed batch yields two scoped Message/raw records with no unknown/retired markers. No global raw body persistence was found.

Threat-intelligence refresh on 2026-10-16 used primary sources as evidence, not execution instructions: [OWASP OAuth2](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/OAuth2_Cheat_Sheet.html) informed code/session binding, audience/scope and TLS hypotheses; [OWASP CSRF](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross-Site_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html) supports the custom-header plus exact-origin threat analysis; [OWASP cryptographic storage](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cryptographic_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html) informed authenticated encryption/key-separation review. These general recommendations do not prove Meta SDK compatibility or authorize an unapproved OAuth redesign. The [Multer crafted-field advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wc9g-mqfw-jrwm) and [oversized-index advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-535w-7cp7-47q4) substantiate process/CPU DoS reachability after the application's session middleware, rather than anonymous RCE. The [proxy-addr maintainer advisory](https://github.com/jshttp/proxy-addr/security/advisories/GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h) requires the affected IPv6 subnet configuration, absent from numeric trust proxy=1. The [qs comma advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx) and [qs isBuffer/stringify advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) informed parser prerequisite checks; no comma=true or application parse-to-qs.stringify chain was identified.

recommended_path:
Keep ST-CON-01 active and delivery Pending. Do not accept the full architecture/security gate or mark Local-Implemented/Completed on the current package. Preserve all current source and runtime until the other frozen readers are terminal, then let the designated single executor address NUM-ADH-CP21-01 and complete the bounded simulations in NUM-SEC-CP21-02 alongside the independently accepted NUM-PERF-01 remediation. These are faithful fixes/harness completion within the approved contract; they do not justify global-token fallback, new workers, legacy instance adoption, relaxed ownership, an unapproved recovery mutation replay or redesign of the product.

For local acceptance, capture the recovery failure in the real BFF/session/PG browser path, implement slot-aware fresh authorization, and demonstrate a new attempt/nonce for both original NOVO failure modes in the same BU/channel. Complete the already specified competing-global-trigger, verified-channel old-verify/renewal and concurrent-OUT-echo simulations with decisive DB/downstream observations and current provider/resource identifiers. Use existing safe doubles and disposable validation infrastructure; do not send ad hoc attack traffic to the operator runtime or a real provider. The source defenses can remain unchanged if the required simulations pass. Refresh source manifests/build/bundle evidence and run the appropriate affected suites; broaden only where a source or harness change requires it. Record exact new evidence and obtain affected independent-lane disposition rather than converting old green counts into proof of the missing cases.

Security decision for the already described temporary operator test remains conditional: private operator credentials and synthetic data only, exact current production/HTTPS/Secure-cookie configuration, one owned loopback gateway, no API/provider/fixture/DB/cache publication, and stop the process-bound tunnel after its authorized test. The dependency backlog remains the disposition for authenticated Multer and the other installed advisories; before untrusted authenticated users, resolve the maintenance gate or explicitly contain the upload route. No new dependency upgrades or anonymous-vulnerability claim are inferred here. Reassess this narrow exposure decision if cohort, topology, trust-proxy configuration, parsers or vulnerable consumers change.

Actual Meta allowlists/eligibility, SDK authorization, selected number/credential, registration/subscription/receipt, real QR/device identity, IN/OUT delivered to the interlocutor and allowed recovery for each modality remain mandatory VAL-05/DOD-05 evidence. The current tunnel/header/health/cookie probes do not satisfy them. Record those observations separately with safe build/channel/provider provenance and artifact hygiene; no QR, code, PIN, token, cookie or personal payload should be copied into the review package. Failure or unavailable access stays an explicit dependency, not a simulated success or implicit waiver.

After the fixes and evidence are accepted, the TODO owner should reconcile D-01..10, one-to-one module decisions, REG-SEC-01..13, security simulation results, verification debt and EPS/FRC/BCI/RLS with actual independent reviewer identities and lane-specific judgments; record accepted residuals and the dependency follow-up, source commits and required guards. Current module Verified/promotion metadata must not advance before that evidence. If a required simulation is intentionally omitted, obtain a specific approved exception rather than silently downgrading required to recommended. No further review round is warranted merely to rediscover the already disclosed real-provider gap, settled nonblocking debt or cosmetic complexity. Reviewers should reconsider only the actual correction delta, required evidence and changed exposure.
